item.text:
**5B.9 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024**

**Bottom line:** *Mostly yes on competence, mixed on honesty.* The strongest evidence shows a government that responded to inflation, food shocks, and disasters with fairly conventional policy tools, and that kept macro indicators broadly within target. The main negative is that rice inflation stayed severe for much of 2024, the government’s initial explanations were partly too simple, and some official messaging was later judged incomplete or inaccurate by independent fact-checking.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `Philippines: 2024 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; and Staff Report` | IMF | 2024-12-19 | [link](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/12/17/pr-24478-philippines-imf-concludes-2024-article-iv-consultation) | The IMF said the Philippines handled multiple external headwinds well, growth stayed resilient, inflation fell from 6.0% in 2023 to 3.2% in 2024, and fiscal consolidation was underway. This is the strongest broad competence signal. | `5B.9`; also `5B.3`, `5B.6` |
| `Philippines: 2024 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; and Staff Report` | IMF | 2024-12-19 | [link](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/12/19/philippines-2024-article-iv-consultation-press-release-and-staff-report-559739) | The staff report says growth recovered, inflation stayed within target, debt was being managed through gradual consolidation, and risks came mainly from commodity volatility, natural disasters, and stalled reforms. This supports competent but not flawless crisis management. | `5B.9`; also `5B.3`, `5B.6` |
| `Unemployment Rate in April 2024 was Estimated at 4.0 Percent` | Philippine Statistics Authority | 2024-06-06 | [link](https://psa.gov.ph/content/unemployment-rate-april-2024-was-estimated-40-percent?vcode=2LnTw) | Unemployment fell to 4.0% in April 2024, below April 2023 and January 2024, but underemployment rose to 14.6%. That is mixed labor-market performance, not a clean success. | `5B.9`; also `5B.6` |
| `PBBM: No need for nationwide state of calamity over El Niño` | Philippine News Agency | 2024-04-08 | [link](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1222231) | Marcos rejected a nationwide calamity declaration and said the response should vary by locality. That suggests a calibrated response rather than blunt overreaction. | `5B.9`; also `5B.6` |
| `Infra dev’t, aid support ramped up as El Niño, La Niña tested PH` | Philippine News Agency | 2024-12-26 | [link](https://www.pna.gov.ph/index.php/articles/1240576) | The report says Marcos responded promptly to El Niño, typhoons, cash aid, food packs, evacuation centers, and flood-control planning. This is strong evidence of active crisis management. | `5B.9`; also `5B.6`, `5B.8` |
| `PBBM: Rice price hike is a global issue` | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-02-25 | [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-rice-price-hike-is-a-global-issue/) | Marcos said rice inflation was a regional/global problem and pointed to external shocks and supply issues, while promising supply and price stabilization. This is honest about external drivers, though it underplays domestic policy failure. | `5B.9`; also `5B.7` |
| `Marcos opens 2024 SONA admitting rice prices are costly` | GMA News Online | 2024-07-22 | [link](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/914278/marcos-opens-2024-sona-admitting-rice-prices-are-costly/story/) | Marcos publicly acknowledged that official statistics meant little to families facing rice at P45-P65/kg. This is direct evidence of candor about inflation pain. | `5B.9`; also `5B.7` |
| `Philippine inflation quickens again in March as rice soars` | Reuters / Investing.com | 2024-04-04 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/philippine-inflation-quickens-again-in-march-as-rice-soars-3366872) | Reuters reported rice inflation hit its fastest pace in 15 years and kept the central bank tight. This shows the shock was severe and not yet under control in early 2024. | `5B.9`; also `5B.3` |
| `Philippine central bank governor rules out easing rates 'soon'` | Reuters / Investing.com | 2024-03-05 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/philippine-central-bank-governor-rules-out-easing-rates-soon-3325861) | The BSP said it was too soon to declare victory over inflation because rice and other food prices were still driving expectations. This is useful counterevidence to any claim of quick stabilization. | `5B.9`; also `5B.3` |
| `NEDA: Reduced rice tariffs failed to lower prices` | GMA News Online | 2024-12-10 | [link](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/money/economy/929579/neda-reduced-rice-tariffs-failed-to-lower-prices/story/) | NEDA said the rice tariff cut did not reduce retail rice prices as anticipated. That undercuts the administration’s earlier claim that the intervention was already working. | `5B.9`; also `5B.7` |
| `PBBM admin made every effort to shield Filipinos from high food prices, keeps inflation within target in 2024` | Department of Finance | 2024-12-17 | [link](https://www.dof.gov.ph/pbbm-admin-made-every-effort-to-shield-filipinos-from-high-food-prices-keeps-inflation-within-target-in-2024/) | DOF said inflation ended 2024 at 3.2%, rice prices moderated, and low-income households benefited after tariff cuts and other interventions. This is positive evidence for competent stabilization, though it is government self-assessment. | `5B.9`; also `5B.3`, `5B.7` |
| `DA: Tariff cut prevented further spike in rice prices` | Philippine News Agency | 2024-12-11 | [link](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1239750) | The DA argued the rice tariff cut prevented even higher prices amid typhoons and a weak peso. This supports the case that the government’s intervention helped absorb shocks. | `5B.9`; also `5B.7` |
| `Sona 2024 fact check` | Philippine Daily Inquirer | 2024-07-23 | [link](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1964296/sona-2024-fact-check) | Independent fact-checkers rated Marcos’s claim that prices were mainly driven by external forces as inaccurate or incomplete, while also finding some rice-output claims correct. This is the best evidence that his public explanation was partly overstated. | `5B.9`; also `5B.7` |
| `2024 average inflation eased to 3.2% as gov’t interventions sustained rice price moderation, benefitting low-income families` | Department of Finance | 2025-01-07 | [link](https://www.dof.gov.ph/recto-2024-average-inflation-eased-to-3-2-as-govt-interventions-sustained-rice-price-moderation-benefitting-low-income-families/) | Looking back at 2024, DOF credited interventions with keeping inflation within target and lowering rice inflation sharply by year-end. This supports a positive final-year stabilization outcome, especially for poorer households. | `5B.9`; also `5B.3`, `5B.8` |
| `Philippines’ budget surplus at P6.3 billion in October` | Reuters / Interaksyon | 2024-11-27 | [link](https://interaksyon.philstar.com/business/2024/11/27/287793/philippines-budget-surplus-at-6-3-billion-in-october/) | The government posted an October budget surplus and narrowed the year-to-date deficit versus the prior year. This is modest positive evidence on fiscal handling, though it is only one month and not a full-year verdict. | `5B.9`; also `5B.3` |
| `Marcos’ cautious economic outlook on El Nino, geopolitical risks` | Reuters / Investing.com | 2024-01-12 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/philippines-marcos-gives-cautious-economic-outlook-on-el-nino-geopolitical-risks-3273028) | Marcos publicly framed the outlook as constrained by El Niño and geopolitical risks and appointed Recto while praising his understanding of the economy. This is a reasonable, non-panicked framing of risk. | `5B.9`; also `5B.2` |

**Synthesis**
- Best competence evidence: IMF assessment, inflation returning to target by year-end, and active disaster/food-price response.
- Best honesty evidence: Marcos acknowledged rice pain directly in his SONA and said the problem had global/external drivers, but independent fact-checking found parts of that explanation incomplete or inaccurate.
- Main weakness: early- and mid-2024 rice inflation remained severe, and tariff cuts did not immediately or cleanly solve the problem.
- Net: Marcos looks materially competent at macro stabilization and crisis response, but his explanation of the rice/inflation problem was sometimes too rosy.

**Search gap**
- I found no meaningful 2024 sanctions episode for the Philippines that would let me judge sanctions management.
- I also found little direct evidence on unemployment policy beyond the labor-market statistics themselves; the record is much stronger on inflation, food shocks, and disaster response than on jobs policy.
